title: Platform handoff stitch notes — weekly standup snapshot
body:
Context:
Quick, informal capture from this week’s platform engineering rotation — focus on cross-cutting handoffs between control plane, routing, auth and quota subsystems. Intended as a short read for on-call engineers and rotation leads. Note format is intentionally fragmentary (meeting-scratchpad style).

Attendance / cadence:
- Time: Tue 2026-09-08 09:30 PDT (30m)
- Regular attendees: Maya (rotation lead), Daniel (routing), Elena (auth), Priya (quotas), Omar (controlplane), guests: SRE on-call (Ash), Solutions eng (Rina)

Topline summary (TL;DR):
- No Sev1s. One degraded token-throttling behavior observed in EU region (short spike, 6m) — likely quota edge-case for bursty reserved customers. Root cause under investigation (see action item Q-1).
- Routing experiment (cplane->edge fallthrough) landed to canary (PR merged) but unexpected cookie persistence behavior observed in Chrome Canary — roll-back on canary until follow-up fix.
- Auth session revalidation optimization shows ~12% CPU reduction on token verify path in bench tests; scheduling staged rollout behind feature flag.

Notes by subteam:
1) Control Plane (Omar)
- Items:
  - cplane PR #318 merged (alloc service: add preferred-zone hint for dedicated pools). Deployed to canary cluster cplane-canary-3.
  - Observed transient 503s from allocator to node-manager during canary traffic spike 2026-09-07 23:14 UTC (6m window). Early hypothesis: node-manager GC cycle + scheduling storm. Logs attached in linked_artifacts.
- Risks/open:
  - If node-manager GC coincides with allocation churn for dedicated pools, we may see higher fallthrough rates — need smoothing.
- Action items:
  - CP-1: Omar to open follow-up GH issue to add backoff on allocator->node-manager calls and add metrics for GC overlap (due 2026-09-14).
  - CP-2: Add a short-run chaos test to simulate GC during allocation churn (owner: Omar / SRE co-owner Ash, due 2026-09-21).

2) Routing (Daniel)
- Items:
  - Fallthrough routing experiment v2 deployed to 10% canary. Observed cookie persistence mismatch for long-lived websocket upgrades in Chrome Canary on path /v1/stream. Investigation points to header rewrites in edge-proxy.
  - Test harness added to synthetic runner to include websocket + sticky cookie scenarios.
- Risks/open:
  - If header rewrite change is applied to all regions, existing client SDK sessions might break.
- Action items:
  - R-1: Daniel to revert routing change on canary today EOD and add instrumentation for cookie header traces (done; canary reverted).
  - R-2: Add integration test with client SDK team (ticket PL-842) to validate session continuity (owner: Daniel, due 2026-09-15).

3) Auth (Elena)
- Items:
  - Bench results for session revalidation optimization: CPU per-verify down 12% at p95 request size for our synthetic workload. Memory neutral.
  - Security review scheduled with InfoSec on 2026-09-10 to confirm no regression on token revocation semantics.
- Risks/open:
  - Small chance of stale revocation cache if rollout not coordinated with revocation-propagation service.
- Action items:
  - A-1: Feature-flag rollout plan to staged clusters + a revocation sweep job after each stage (owner: Elena, due 2026-09-18).
  - A-2: Add dashboard panel for revocation-latency per-region (owner: Elena / Observability, due 2026-09-16).

4) Quotas (Priya)
- Items:
  - Investigating a quota enforcement corner-case: bursty reserved-tier customers in EU cause short lived token-throttle spikes — throttles overlap with reserved-capacity burst policy and lead to 429s even when reserved capacity available.
  - Captured traces for one affected customer session (attached to PL ticket).
- Risks/open:
  - Unclear if the burst credit deduction calculation double-counts prefetched tokens across gateway and controlplane.
- Action items:
  - Q-1: Priya to reproduce in integration harness with reserved-tier burst scenario and create minimal repro. If repro matches, file fix PR to adjust burst-credit accounting (owner: Priya, due 2026-09-13).
  - Q-2: Add a post-mortem mini-runbook for common quota edgecases (owner: Priya, due 2026-09-20).

Cross-team coordination and blockers:
- SRE notes: recommended throttle smoothing of allocator calls to avoid node-manager contention (aligns with CP-1).
- Observability request: need token-level tracing across routing->auth->quota for the failing EU sessions. Requesting short-lived trace-id propagation header (opt-in) to be added to canary (owner: Daniel + Elena, due 2026-09-11).
- Solutions eng: flagged one enterprise customer who reported 429s during a weekend spike (customer-facing ticket CE-553). Suggested immediate customer workaround: bump reserved burst window until repro fixed. Ops agreed to notify customer.

Decisions made during standup:
- Revert routing fallthrough change on canary until client-SDK verified (decision owner: Daniel).
- Prioritize quota repro (Q-1) ahead of non-blocking controlplane smoothing work.

Mini action table (single-line items):
- CP-1: Omar -> open GH issue for allocator backoff + metrics (2026-09-14)
- CP-2: Omar + Ash -> schedule GC-chaos test (2026-09-21)
- R-1: Daniel -> revert canary & add cookie traces (DONE 2026-09-08)
- R-2: Daniel -> client-SDK integration test (PL-842) (2026-09-15)
- A-1: Elena -> staged rollout + revocation sweep job (2026-09-18)
- A-2: Elena -> revocation-latency panel (2026-09-16)
- Q-1: Priya -> repro reserved-burst 429 and PR if needed (2026-09-13)
- Q-2: Priya -> quota edgecase runbook (2026-09-20)

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- Do we propagate an opt-in trace header across client SDKs to make quota/auth cross-correlation easier? (cost vs privacy tradeoff)
- Should burst-credit accounting be moved entirely to edge-proxy for simpler semantics? (needs performance/scale analysis)

Extras / notes to self:
- Follow-up threads to start: add a short Slack channel #pl-routing-auth-quota for async updates on Q-1 / R-2 / A-1.
- Keep customer success in the loop for CE-553; Priya to draft a short status note for Monday 2026-09-13.

Appendix (metrics snapshot observed during meeting):
- Controlplane alloc latency (p50/p95): 12ms / 87ms (canary spike window p95 -> 240ms)
- Routing error rate on canary: 0.3% -> after revert: 0.05%
- Auth verify CPU (perf bench): baseline 1.0 -> optimized 0.88 (relative)
- Quota 429 rate EU (last 24h): baseline 0.02% -> spike window 0.45% (6m)

If you’re on rotation next week and want to pick up any of the open owners above, reply inline in this doc or ping me in Slack.

Short link to follow-ups: CON-241 (design), PL-842 (integration test), GH #318 (merged).

-- Maya
2026-09-09
